newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wheelock says new habits hit S'pore retail.
newsitem.headline: Wheelock says new habits hit S'pore retail.

text.p: Top managers of Wheelock And Co Ltd on Tuesday blamed the closure of its upmarket Lane Crawford retail department store in Singapore on declining tourist arrivals and changing shopping habits.
"Singapore's tourism market is not enough to sustain shopping...shopping has been decentralised outward to regional areas," managing director John Hung said at a news conference.
Hong Kong conglomerate Wheelock holds 74 percent of Lane Crawford A shares and 66 percent of B shares.
The retailer pulls the shutters over its departmental store in Singapore, sited at a prominent crossroad along the island's Orchard Road shopping belt, at the end of September.
Lane Crawford, which sustained a HK$40 million operating loss over the past six months, said earlier it would suspend its regional expansion following the Singapore experience.
Large, one-stop shopping complexes have sprouted in Singapore's various housing neighbourhoods in recent years, moving shoppers away from the main Orchard shopping belt.
Compounded with a general slowdown in Singapore's retail market and sluggish tourist arrivals, other retailers are hurting just as much, chairman Gonzaga Li said.
"The retail market is now quite slow for everyone, even Japanese stores. Lane Crawford is not an exception," Li said.
Singapore's property market rang a more cheery note, where Wheelock's Ardmore Park development has been well-received.
More than 210 of the 220 residential units offered in July were snapped up within a week and Li said the company might offer the remaining 104 units in early 1997.
In Hong Kong, Wheelock would be offering units in its 2,000-unit Diamond Hill residential development in 1997.
